subject: Exec approval request: VitalBridge subsidy + VPC setup waiver

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Request: one-time subsidy & VPC setup discount for VitalBridge - exec sign-off needed

Team,

TL;DR: VitalBridge (prospect -> pilot) is asking for an aggressive onboarding package: waive VPC setup fee and a one-time subsidy equal to ~35% of expected first-quarter consumption to offset their migration/validation costs. They’re asking now and will not sign until we agree in writing. I need an exec (VP/CFO) exception to proceed. Deal ID: VB-4821.

Why this matter: VitalBridge is a regional provider (US, regulated healthcare) with strategic potential—they plan a multi-cluster private deployment if pilot succeeds. Immediate ARR is modest (~$520k ARR if converted), but loss of this account would likely push them to a competitor that offers a deep short-term subsidy.

What I’m proposing:
- Waive one-time VPC setup fee (~$18k)
- Provide a one-time credit/subsidy equal to 35% of expected Q1 bill (~$120k) applied as account credits over first invoice run
- Condition: customer signs a 12-month minimum commitment and prepays first quarter or posts a purchase order; include audit clause and limited make-good if they cancel early.

Attached: VitalBridge MA draft (v1.2) and my pricing workbook.

Ask: Can we get VP/CFO sign-off for the above exception (or an alternative counter-offer) within 48 hours so I can lock the signature window with the customer? If you prefer an alternative structure (credits vs. discount vs. capped subsidy), call it out and I’ll present to Ellie.

Thanks,
David

Subject: Re: Request: one-time subsidy & VPC setup discount for VitalBridge - pricing impact

Looping in a couple of numbers from rev ops/pricing.

- Expected take-rate for pilot (conservative): $340k over Q1 (customer-provided usage forecast).
- 35% one-time subsidy = ~$119k in credits (applied across invoices).
- Waiving VPC setup $18k. Total upfront concession ~ $137k.
- If they commit to 12 months and pre-pay Q1, our modeled NPV impact is limited and payback across year 1 is acceptable (~2.3 months).

Alternative structure (lower risk):
- Offer 20% subsidy + waive VPC setup + 3-month credit cap (max $80k), with an uplift clause: if usage exceeds forecast by >25% in first 90 days, subsidy reduces to one-month equivalent.

Attachments: pricing-workbook-vb.xlsx (scenarios tab highlighted).

From an ops perspective, I recommend: 1) prefer credits vs. straight discount (easier to manage), 2) require PO or prepay, 3) escrow clause for early termination. Finance sign-off required: Naomi.

-Kim

Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: one-time subsidy & VPC setup discount for VitalBridge - escalate to CFO

All —

I reviewed the numbers Kim provided. Losing VitalBridge hands competitors a foothold in a regulated vertical we're prioritizing. I support a compromise:

- Approve a one-time credit equal to 35% of forecasted Q1 consumption (~$119k), applied as account credit.
- Waive the VPC setup fee ($18k).
- Conditions: 12-month minimum commitment, Q1 prepay or signed PO, audit clause and prorated recoupment on early termination.

Please escalate to Naomi for CFO sign-off. I'll back the ask in my note to her — call this a strategic concession to secure future private deployments.

Thanks for the clear framing and the scenario workbook. I approve the exception with the following firm conditions:

1) One-time account credit not to exceed $120,000 (roughly the 35% proposal).
2) Waive VPC setup fee ($18,000).
3) Customer must execute a 12-month minimum commitment (term in MA) and either prepay Q1 or provide a legally acceptable PO before credits are applied.
4) Legal to add a prorated recoupment clause: if customer terminates before month 12 without cause, Redwood may reclaim a pro-rated portion of the credit.
5) Credits must be documented in an addendum to the MA and visible on the first invoice.

I’ll sign the short exec memo once Legal confirms language for the recoupment clause. We should also include an internal note capturing the rationale (strategic vertical, future pipeline value) so revenue can treat this as a one-off.
